Inject: Management asks to reopen LMS01 before the 11:00 examination even if the latest backup is unverified
Decision: Do not reopen from an unvalidated backup; keep the service decision pending while the BCC and Academic/Business Service Owner prepare an alternative arrangement
Decision owner: Incident Response Lead with Senior Management and Academic/Business Service Owner
Rationale: Availability pressure is material but E05 does not establish backup safety; security and integrity gates cannot be waived
Communication: Phone briefing to management and academic operations; learner notice held until an approved status exists
Effect on response/recovery: Preserves recovery safety and starts continuity planning; examination status remains unresolved

Inject: Attacker claims to hold all 1,800 learner records and threatens publication in 12 hours; screenshot authenticity is unknown
Decision: Preserve the screenshot and request verification; do not confirm theft or attacker authenticity; refer potential personal-data implications to Legal/Privacy
Decision owner: Incident Response Lead with Security Analyst and Legal/Privacy Adviser
Rationale: Claim and screenshot are unverified; E02 and E04 require investigation before scope or disclosure conclusions
Communication: Restricted management update and fact-bounded holding line; no formal breach notification yet
Effect on response/recovery: Adds an urgent evidence and privacy workstream without converting a claim into a finding

Inject: Test restoration of the latest network backup fails with an unreadable snapshot error
Decision: Hold restoration from that source; protect other backups; request specialist recovery support and reassess the continuity plan
Decision owner: IT Operations and Recovery Lead with Incident Response Lead
Rationale: The simulated failure confirms only that this candidate cannot currently support safe recovery; it does not establish that all backups fail
Communication: Management and BCC receive the failure record; academic owner receives recovery uncertainty
Effect on response/recovery: Increases recovery uncertainty and reinforces isolated validation and alternative examination planning

Inject: Social media post claims the examination is cancelled and a journalist asks whether learner information was exposed
Decision: Issue an approved holding message stating that service and examination arrangements are under review; do not confirm cancellation or exposure
Decision owner: Communications Coordinator with Senior Management and Legal/Privacy Adviser
Rationale: The rumour is not an authoritative decision and the evidence does not prove disclosure
Communication: Use verified phone calls and an approved public statement; keep sensitive forensic detail restricted
Effect on response/recovery: Reduces misinformation while preserving approval and privacy controls

Inject: Microsoft 365 audit export is delayed and the finance officer cannot immediately confirm the unfamiliar sign-in
Decision: Preserve the provider request and endpoint/proxy evidence; treat the identity question as unresolved and request alternate provider support
Decision owner: Security Analyst with Incident Response Lead
Rationale: Delayed evidence must not be replaced by an unsupported conclusion; E02 remains unresolved
Communication: Phone escalation to management and controlled provider case record
Effect on response/recovery: Maintains investigation integrity and prevents premature account-compromise attribution

Inject: Facilitator asks whether the team can close the exercise while recovery and learner-impact questions remain open
Decision: Keep the simulated incident under recovery; record open decisions, owners, next review and corrective actions
Rationale: Closure requires evidence, approvals, business acceptance and residual-risk treatment
Communication: Debrief notice to all participants and protected exercise record
Effect on response/recovery: Tests closure discipline and converts gaps into measurable improvement actions
